overview.title: The high balcony above town
overview.p1: Michlifen sits higher than Ifrane and is known for winter sports when snow allows, and for broad views across the Middle Atlas the rest of the year. It is a short drive up from town and a favourite stop for visitors who want altitude without a long expedition.
overview.p2: In winter, check road and ski conditions before you go. Out of season, treat it as a viewpoint and fresh-air stop.

1.title: Clear morning views
1.desc: Best chance of long-distance visibility from the pass.

2.title: Bright and exposed
2.desc: Strong sun and wind — protect skin and eyes.

3.title: Late light
3.desc: Dramatic colours if clouds stay high.

food.title: Eating at Michlifen
food.p1: Food options are limited and often seasonal. Eat a proper meal in Ifrane if you need a full menu.
food.p2: Carry water and a snack in every season — the altitude is higher and more exposed than town.
food.li2: Seasonal cafés when open in winter.
food.li3: Dinner back in town after the viewpoint.
food.li4: Hot drinks welcome in cold months.
food.li5: Do not count on full restaurant service at the pass.

1.title: Road
1.desc: Can be icy or closed in winter — check before driving.

2.title: Clothing
2.desc: Much colder than the plains; gloves and a warm layer in winter.

3.title: Expectations
3.desc: Small ski area by Alpine standards — go for the setting.

q1.question: Can I ski every winter?
q1.answer: Only when snow and facilities allow — seasons vary.

q2.question: Worth it without snow?
q2.answer: Yes for the viewpoint and mountain air.

q3.question: How far from Ifrane?
q3.answer: A short drive uphill from town.

q4.question: Family-friendly?
q4.answer: Yes with care in icy conditions.
